records.title: Misdiagnosed centipede and scorpion poisoning characterized by delayed hypersensitivity reaction: A case report.
records.case_context: A 38-year-old woman had cough and fever for more than 10 days, failed anti-infective treatment, and later developed a rash. A more detailed medication history raised concern for centipede and scorpion exposure from traditional Chinese medicine.
records.intervention: She received anti-allergic treatment with methylprednisolone and loratadine after delayed hypersensitivity was diagnosed.
records.outcome: The report states that symptoms resolved and no recurrent fever or rash was reported during one year of follow-up.
records.reasoning_use: Teach the model to revisit medication and herbal exposure when an initial infectious explanation fails, and to treat TCM adverse effects as part of the differential rather than assuming benefit.

records.title: Non-occupational lead poisoning associated with traditional Chinese medicine: A case report.
records.case_context: A 21-year-old man with severe periumbilical colic had anemia and liver injury. Careful history revealed about one year of traditional Chinese medicine use for acne, and blood lead concentration was markedly elevated.
records.intervention: The patient received chelation treatment for lead poisoning.
records.outcome: The report describes recovery after treatment.
records.reasoning_use: Train safety reasoning: obtain exposure history, connect objective toxicology findings with possible herbal contamination, and avoid assuming traditional medicines are intrinsically low-risk.

records.title: Strychnine poisoning due to traditional Chinese medicine: a case series.
records.case_context: A Hong Kong case series reviewed 12 laboratory-confirmed strychnine poisonings; Strychni semen was the identified source in all cases, with muscle spasms and conscious convulsions among common presentations.
records.intervention: Management varied by poisoning severity; the report emphasizes timely recognition and supportive/toxicology care.
records.outcome: No fatalities were reported in the series.
records.reasoning_use: Use as a multi-case safety pattern: recognize characteristic toxidrome, ask specifically about TCM/herbal exposure, and distinguish safety surveillance from therapeutic reasoning.

records.title: Arsenical keratosis in China: A case report and review of the literature.
records.case_context: The report and review describe arsenical keratosis associated with chronic arsenic exposure, with traditional Chinese medicine identified as a major iatrogenic source in the reviewed Chinese cases.
records.intervention: Management in the reviewed literature included stopping arsenic exposure, dermatologic surveillance, acitretin for keratotic lesions, and tumor-directed treatments when malignancy occurred.
records.outcome: The review found frequent hyperkeratotic and pigmentary skin changes and reported skin tumors in a substantial subset of cases.
records.reasoning_use: Teach long-latency adverse-effect reasoning, source attribution, and the need for malignancy surveillance without converting review frequencies into patient-specific predictions.

records.title: Successful conservative treatment of placenta accreta with traditional Chinese medicine: A case report.
records.case_context: A 37-year-old postpartum woman had persistent vaginal bleeding and imaging findings consistent with retained placenta accreta. Doppler ultrasound and beta-hCG supported the diagnosis, and an attempted curettage was stopped because of excessive bleeding.
records.intervention: The report describes subsequent conservative treatment with a multi-herbal traditional Chinese medicine formula.
records.outcome: Residual placental tissue was reported to have been expelled after four months, with resolution of symptoms and no reported complications during short follow-up.
records.reasoning_use: Teach the model to prioritize obstetric diagnosis and bleeding risk, identify the conservative-management context, and avoid generalizing a single successful case into a standard recommendation.

records.title: A case report of effective treatment of intracranial atherosclerotic stenosis treated with the integration of traditional Chinese medicine and Western medicine.
records.case_context: A 39-year-old man with transient ischemic attack, headache and dizziness was diagnosed with intracranial atherosclerotic stenosis using noninvasive vascular imaging.
records.intervention: Western risk-factor and antiplatelet management was combined with syndrome-differentiated Chinese herbal treatment.
records.outcome: Follow-up imaging in the report described reduced stenosis/plaque findings and improved flow measurements.
records.reasoning_use: Train layered reasoning around established vascular diagnosis, objective imaging follow-up, multimodal treatment, and the inability of one case to establish treatment efficacy.

records.title: Fungal keratitis treated with a combination of traditional Chinese medicine and Western medicine: A case report.
records.case_context: A 56-year-old man had painful blurred vision with a large corneal ulcer. In vivo confocal microscopy demonstrated inflammatory infiltration and fungal hyphae, supporting fungal keratitis.
records.intervention: After poor response and adverse effects with initial Western treatment, the report describes adding a traditional Chinese medicine decoction in an integrated approach.
records.outcome: After 21 days the ulcer was described as shallower with improved vision and relief of discomfort, although long-term follow-up was unavailable.
records.reasoning_use: Teach that microbiologic/ophthalmic evidence establishes the diagnosis, while treatment interpretation must preserve the missing long-term follow-up and single-case limitation.

records.title: Integrated treatment utilizing both Chinese and Western medicine for refractory diabetic foot ulcers: a case report.
records.case_context: A 57-year-old man with a Wagner grade IV diabetic foot ulcer continued to deteriorate despite two toe amputations and had poorly controlled diabetes.
records.intervention: An integrated plan combined oral/topical TCM with glycemic control, anti-infective therapy, circulation support, anticoagulation, neurotrophic and nutritional management.
records.outcome: Across 144 days the report described near-complete closure at discharge, later epithelialization and functional recovery, with HbA1c improvement.
records.reasoning_use: Teach complex multimodal case reasoning in which metabolic control, infection management and wound care remain explicit contributors; do not attribute the outcome to one component alone.

records.title: How to continue lipid-lowering therapy in patients with coronary heart disease and severe liver dysfunction?: A case report of plaque regression by a combination of Chinese and Western Medicine.
records.case_context: A 36-year-old man with exertional chest pain had about 60% proximal LAD stenosis and severe liver enzyme elevation in the setting of hepatitis B, complicating usual lipid-lowering therapy.
records.intervention: The report describes a Chinese medicine-based lipid-lowering and syndrome-differentiated approach alongside cardiovascular management because statin therapy was limited by liver dysfunction.
records.outcome: Symptoms and liver enzymes improved and follow-up coronary CT angiography was reported without the prior proximal LAD stenosis.
records.reasoning_use: Teach contraindication-aware treatment reasoning and objective follow-up while avoiding the conclusion that the reported alternative is equivalent to standard lipid-lowering therapy.

records.title: Extensive small cell lung cancer treated by integrated traditional Chinese and Western medicine: A case report.
records.case_context: A 68-year-old man had biopsy-confirmed extensive-stage small cell lung cancer with nodal and bilateral lung metastases.
records.intervention: The published regimen combined chemotherapy and radiotherapy with several traditional Chinese herbal prescriptions and supportive antiemetic treatment.
records.outcome: The report describes disappearance of lesions on follow-up imaging, return to normal daily activity and no recurrence at four years.
records.reasoning_use: Train the model to keep biopsy and imaging as diagnostic anchors, recognize multi-component oncology care, and avoid attributing a durable response to the herbal component from a single case.

records.title: Favorable effect of herbal extract on androgenic alopecia: A case report.
records.case_context: A 41-year-old man had an eight-year history of moderate androgenic alopecia.
records.intervention: The report describes three months of a topical aqueous spray containing several herbal extracts.
records.outcome: Trichoscopy-based measures were reported to show increased hair density and changes in hair diameter and related metrics.
records.reasoning_use: Teach objective-before/after measurement extraction and the distinction between a promising single-patient observation and validated efficacy.

records.title: Traditional Chinese medicine for premature ventricular contraction caused by obstructive sleep apnea: A case report and literature review.
records.case_context: A 37-year-old man with obstructive sleep apnea and persistent premature ventricular contractions had ongoing palpitations despite ventilatory support and propafenone. Other common causes of PVC were reportedly excluded.
records.intervention: A modified Huanglian Wendan Decoction was added within the existing treatment plan.
records.outcome: The report states that 24-hour Holter PVC count fell from 8968 to zero after 21 days and symptoms improved, with later reduction and discontinuation of propafenone.
records.reasoning_use: Teach causal caution: record the objective Holter change and concurrent therapies, but do not infer that one case proves TCM treatment for OSA-related arrhythmia.

records.title: Successful delivery in a cornual pregnancy after expectant management with traditional Chinese medicine and low-molecular-weight heparin: A case report.
records.case_context: A 32-year-old woman with painless vaginal bleeding had transvaginal ultrasound findings confirming cornual pregnancy and strongly wished to preserve the pregnancy.
records.intervention: After extensive consultation she underwent expectant management with low-molecular-weight heparin and traditional Chinese medicine.
records.outcome: Serial ultrasound reportedly showed stable fetal development and the pregnancy ended in successful cesarean delivery.
records.reasoning_use: Teach high-risk obstetric reasoning: foreground rupture risk and diagnostic imaging, represent the unusual conservative pathway accurately, and avoid converting a rare successful case into routine advice.

records.title: Persistent cough due to cough variant asthma following upper respiratory tract infection treated by traditional Chinese medicine: A case report.
records.case_context: A patient with cough-variant asthma had persistent cough after an upper respiratory infection and suboptimal response/adherence to conventional treatment. The TCM pattern was described as wind-heat offending the lung.
records.intervention: The report describes an individualized Chinese herbal decoction aimed at clearing heat, dispelling wind and relieving cough.
records.outcome: After two weeks, symptom scores and several small-airway function measures were reported to improve without observed laboratory safety abnormalities.
records.reasoning_use: Teach symptom-plus-objective-function reasoning and preserve the report's own statement that larger rigorous studies are needed before generalization.
